title: Print Header Footer Navbar Spacing Parity
description: In the Zwischenbericht mit Bestand print report, the header (navbar) and footer chrome spacing no longer matches the on-screen app UI's navbar/footer spacing. The header currently has too little vertical spacing (too cramped) and the footer has way too much spacing (too much gap). Need to bring both back into parity with the app UI's navbar/footer padding, likely by adjusting headsep/footskip and/or internal chrome bar padding in print/tex/semio-window.sty (see SemioChromeNavbarHead, SemioChromeFooterHead, headsep=\semio@spacing@double, semio@chrome@footer@reserve computation around line 2621-2634).
summary:
Fourth and final follow-up: found the actual root cause of the persistent chip-touches-rule issue that survived three previous "fixes" in this ticket.

`\semio@chrome@row@height` (and `row@height@footer`) was used for two conflicting purposes at once in print/tex/semio-window.sty: (1) sizing the inner `\semio@chrome@vcenter{row@height}{...}` box that centers the *bare* icon/text before it gets wrapped in a chip, and (2) sizing the *outer* `\semio@chrome@bar@threezone{row@height}{...}` zone box that contains the *fully chip-wrapped* content (bare content + `\semio@chrome@chip`'s own `\fcolorbox` padding + border). Since the chip wrapper always adds `2×padding + 2×hairline` on top of whatever it wraps, the fully-wrapped chip *always* overflowed the threezone's box by exactly that amount (≈5.88pt) — confirmed via `\savebox`+`\the\ht`/`\the\dp` debug instrumentation (`fullchip` measured 13.08pt vs a 7.2pt target). This overflow is invisible to LaTeX's own box-size bookkeeping (a `\vbox to <target>` always *reports* exactly `<target>` regardless of internal overflow — confirmed this is why `\SemioChromeNavbarHead`'s own outer measurement always showed a "clean" 20.46pt with zero depth even while overflowing internally) — so the ink from the overflowing chip bled straight through my `\vskip\semio@spacing@single` gap (added in the second fix) and into the rule, no matter how that gap was implemented (vfil, vskip, or dimexpr — all tested and ruled out as the cause). Every prior fix in this ticket (the row@height formula change, the headheight revert, the vfil/vskip anchoring) was necessary but not sufficient on its own; none addressed this specific double-use-of-one-length structural issue, and reverting the row@height formula along the way (in this session) made it briefly worse before this proper split fixed it for good.

Fixed by splitting the single `row@height` into two lengths: `\semio@chrome@row@height`/`row@height@footer` (reverted back to just the bare font size, used only for the inner vcenter) and new `\semio@chrome@zone@height`/`zone@height@footer` (= row@height + 2×padding + 2×hairline, matching the *real* fully-wrapped chip height) — the latter now passed to `\semio@chrome@bar@threezone` instead of `row@height`. Also updated the public `\SemioChromeIconSize`/`\SemioChromeFooterIconSize` API to keep `zone@height`/`zone@height@footer` in sync when a caller changes the icon size. Removed the `\savebox`/`\typeout` debug instrumentation used to diagnose this.

Verified via `--skip-nx-cache` rebuilds of the real mit-bestand zwischenbericht document and all print/dist templates: zero "Overfull \vbox (5.87991pt too high)" warnings (previously appeared on every page), zero fancyhdr "headheight is too small" warnings, and rasterized crops confirm the navbar chips/icon now sit with a clean, visible gap above their rule — a true mirror of the footer's gap below its rule — on both scrreprt and scrartcl templates.
